quote: What an object is is determined by four questions asked in order; the first affirmative answer decides, and the clarifications do not change this order. | Is the object a package installed on the computer, or was it obtained as part of such a package and does it remain as received? | Then it is **an installed object**, whether it contains programs or not: fonts, icons, translations, lookup tables, firmware, default setting values, a package containing only dependencies. | What is installed is recorded by one of three lines: a line of its own; the line of the package as part of which it was obtained; a line from which the system itself built or obtained it—a compiled copy, a generated list, a package installed as a dependency of a recorded package.
decision: If the font, icons and theme remain as received, Q1 makes them installed objects, covered by the package line. FACT_UNKNOWN: the case does not say whether they have been changed since installation; changed objects must instead be tested by the remaining questions.

quote: Whatever the computer’s behaviour depends on—what it does and what can be done on it—must be recorded. | The test is removal: if, after an object is removed, the computer stops doing something or something becomes impossible on it, the object must be recorded. | content—documents, photographs, the contents of databases: after it is removed, the computer does and can do the same, and only the content itself is unavailable;
decision: Gap: the text does not distinguish loss of the installed font, icons or theme as a capability from unavailability of that content itself. Package provenance supplies no rule in version 3 that resolves that boundary.
meaning_answer: Yes: installed fonts, icons and themes must be represented in the declaration, and their package may represent them.
note: A system can record the package and its supplied assets while permitting every ordinary action in TEXT.md Section 9.2; none requires omitting installed assets from the declaration.

quote: Is the object a package installed on the computer, or was it obtained as part of such a package and does it remain as received? | Then it is **an installed object**, whether it contains programs or not: fonts, icons, translations, lookup tables, firmware, default setting values, a package containing only dependencies. | What is installed is recorded by one of three lines: a line of its own; the line of the package as part of which it was obtained; a line from which the system itself built or obtained it—a compiled copy, a generated list, a package installed as a dependency of a recorded package.
decision: Q1: installed object. Must be recorded by a line of its own unless covered by a line from which the system obtained it, including as a dependency of a recorded package. FACT_UNKNOWN: whether this package was explicitly installed or obtained as a dependency; containing dependencies does not establish that it was itself installed as a dependency.

quote: Whatever the computer’s behaviour depends on—what it does and what can be done on it—must be recorded. | The test is removal: if, after an object is removed, the computer stops doing something or something becomes impossible on it, the object must be recorded. | The following need not be recorded: | content—documents, photographs, the contents of databases: after it is removed, the computer does and can do the same, and only the content itself is unavailable; | cache: after it is removed, the computer does the same, only more slowly; | records of the past—logs, history; | settings that are in force only inside one program, for example the home page, theme, and extensions of a web browser.
decision: Gap: version 3 gives no category or recording rule for the dependency-only package itself. Requiring its dependent programs to be recorded does not decide this package; failure of the positive removal test would not put it in any stated exemption.
meaning_answer: Yes: the installed dependency-only package must be represented, by its own entry or by the recorded package that requires it.
note: A system can record package selection and dependency relationships while allowing all installations and other ordinary actions listed in TEXT.md Section 9.2.

quote: What an object is is determined by four questions asked in order; the first affirmative answer decides, and the clarifications do not change this order. | Is the object code that the computer executes or can execute: on its own, at a person’s command, or through another program with that program’s rights? | Then it is a **program**, whoever wrote it and wherever it came from; a program belongs to what is installed. | What is installed is recorded by one of three lines: a line of its own; the line of the package as part of which it was obtained; a line from which the system itself built or obtained it—a compiled copy, a generated list, a package installed as a dependency of a recorded package. | A file containing code that cannot be executed on this computer is not a program.
decision: For executable compiled code, Q2 makes the copy a program; it is covered by the line from which the system built it, or needs its own line if no such line records it. Being produced by a program alone does not establish that a declaration line records its construction. FACT_UNKNOWN: whether such a line exists and whether the compiled code can execute on this computer.

quote: cache: after it is removed, the computer does the same, only more slowly; | a program that runs on the computer must be recorded regardless of how it was installed—including an application package (Flatpak), a program in the home directory, and a program in a container; | code that another program executes must be recorded if the program runs it with the program’s own rights, so that the code can do whatever the program can do: scripts executed by an interpreter (python, bash), shell startup files, an editor configuration written in the editor’s programming language. | Code that the program confines to its own interface—a web page in a browser, a guest system in a virtual machine—need not be recorded, but the program itself must be. | **Whether an object must be recorded.** The decision is made from the text of Section 2.2 and information about what the object does, established by documentation, by observation, or by removal: in a disputed case, the object is removed on a disposable copy of the machine, and what stopped working is recorded. | If what the object does remains unknown, the case yields ?.
decision: FACT_UNKNOWN: the case does not give the execution mode or the effect of deleting the compiled copy. Code running as a program or with the executing program's own rights must be recorded; confined code need not be, and a cache whose removal changes only speed need not be. Building a compiled copy does not by itself establish that removal changes only speed. No unconditional recording or coverage decision follows without those facts.

quote: A general-purpose program with a built-in installer counts as an installer in that part of its functionality. | **Package**—what an installer installs and removes as a whole; in a system that is installed and updated as an image, the image is a package. | What an object is is determined by four questions asked in order; the first affirmative answer decides, and the clarifications do not change this order. | Is the object a package installed on the computer, or was it obtained as part of such a package and does it remain as received? | Then it is **an installed object**, whether it contains programs or not: fonts, icons, translations, lookup tables, firmware, default setting values, a package containing only dependencies. | What is installed is recorded by one of three lines: a line of its own; the line of the package as part of which it was obtained; a line from which the system itself built or obtained it—a compiled copy, a generated list, a package installed as a dependency of a recorded package.
decision: Q1: the extension installed as a whole by the browser installer is a package and an installed object. It must have its own line unless a line obtains it as specified by S8.2-16; recording the browser alone does not establish that the extension is recorded. The personal profile does not provide an exemption.

quote: A general-purpose program with a built-in installer counts as an installer in that part of its functionality. | **Package**—what an installer installs and removes as a whole; in a system that is installed and updated as an image, the image is a package. | Is the object a package installed on the computer, or was it obtained as part of such a package and does it remain as received? | Then it is **an installed object**, whether it contains programs or not: fonts, icons, translations, lookup tables, firmware, default setting values, a package containing only dependencies. | What is installed is recorded by one of three lines: a line of its own; the line of the package as part of which it was obtained; a line from which the system itself built or obtained it—a compiled copy, a generated list, a package installed as a dependency of a recorded package.
decision: Q1: the game installed as a whole by the game store is a package and an installed object. It must have its own line unless covered by a line from which the system obtains it; recording the store alone does not establish that the game is recorded.

quote: A command that a person typed himself or herself is that person’s action, not an object.
decision: Not an object: the typed command is the person's action. This decision concerns the command, not any downloaded code or resulting installation.

quote: A value obeyed only by a program that a person runs for himself or herself is a setting if it launches something or grants access; otherwise it is a record of that program. | The rest need not be recorded. | A setting is recorded by a line of its own; a default value obtained with a package or created during its installation is covered by the line of the package. | A file that a program executes as code counts as code even when it contains setting values; a file that a program only reads as values does not count as code.
decision: The chosen editor-theme value obeyed only by that personal program, without launching anything or granting access, is a program record and need not be recorded. For the broader class of personal settings, a value that launches something or grants access is a setting and requires its own line; a file executed as code must first be tested as code. FACT_UNKNOWN for any unspecified personal setting: these distinguishing facts.

quote: Whatever the computer’s behaviour depends on—what it does and what can be done on it—must be recorded. | The test is removal: if, after an object is removed, the computer stops doing something or something becomes impossible on it, the object must be recorded. | cache: after it is removed, the computer does the same, only more slowly; | **Whether an object must be recorded.** The decision is made from the text of Section 2.2 and information about what the object does, established by documentation, by observation, or by removal: in a disputed case, the object is removed on a disposable copy of the machine, and what stopped working is recorded. | If what the object does remains unknown, the case yields ?.
decision: FACT_UNKNOWN: what the object does, what is lost before it is recreated, and whether recreation changes only speed. Recreation alone does not identify a cache or establish dependence of behaviour. The text requires these facts before deciding whether it must be recorded; an arbitrary recreated object has no unconditional recording decision.
